slides.texte_overlay:
How to become unbelievably
good at small talk
Start with the place, not the person. "This place has the best music." Comments about where you both are feel natural, easy and never too personal.
Turn yes/no answers into stories. When someone asks "Good weekend?", say "Great, I tried surfing for the first time and fell twenty times." Now there's something to talk about.
Ask about what they're looking forward to. "Any plans for the holidays?" Future plans are light, positive and almost always lead somewhere fun and personal.
Remember one detail and use it at the end. "Good luck with the marathon!" It turns a five-minute chat into something people remember fondly for weeks.
Always have something new. I do five minutes a day of history, art or science, and small talk gets easy when you've got a fresh story ready every week.
slides.texte_sophia: I do five minutes a day on a micro-learning app like the Sophia app. History, art, science. Small talk gets easy when you've got a fresh story every week.

slides.texte_overlay: Give a little before you ask. Share a small thing about yourself first, then ask. People open up more easily when you've opened up a little bit too.
Laugh easily. Small talk isn't a test. A relaxed laugh at a light joke makes the whole conversation feel easy, warm and natural for everyone involved.
